newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hoogovens develops car parts technology.
newsitem.headline: Hoogovens develops car parts technology.

text.p: Dutch metals group Hoogovens said on Tuesday its steel unit had signed an agreement with Germany's Dr. Meleghy GmbH & Co to develop new hydroforming technology, used to manufacture automobile parts.

The new metal forming technique, which uses fluid under high pressure to form complex shaped car parts, results in weight and cost reduction, lower investments and higher quality, Hoogovens said in a statement.
"The agreement reached between both companies is a reaction to projected increasing demand for hydroformed parts," it said.
No financial details of the proposed cooperation were given.
Hoogovens said it would contribute its R&D knowledge in the field of material properties and technologies and Dr. Meleghy its experience in design and manufacture of hydroformed parts.
The first results will be available at the end of the year.

Dr. Meleghy has plants in Germany and Hungary and lists its main customers as Ford, Volkswagen, Mercedes Benz, Opel, BMW and Audi. Hoogovens' main automobile customers are Ford, Volkswagen, Renault, PSA Peugeot Citroen, Volvo, Rover and Fiat.
